To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a murine solid tumor line, 16C, was found to be sensitive to Adriamycin and that the development of resistance was accompanied by a 1.6-fold increase in glutathione content, a 4.7-fold increase in GSH S-transferases and a 2.4-fold increase in GSSG peroxidases.

a spontaneously originated murine adenocarcinomatous mammary tumor, 16C, selected for its sensitivity and responsiveness to agents active against human breast cancer in vivo, has been shown to develop a degree of resistance to Adriacyclin (ADR) in vivo that appears to be mediated through a mechanism that is not directly related to the elevated GSH levels in the tumor cells.

a murine mammary tumor model, selected for sensitivity to agents active in human breast cancer, exhibits a resistance to ADR that is independent of the well characterized mdr phenotype, and that is associated with elevated levels of GSH and GSH S-transferases and peroxidases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental model of ADR resistance in the 16C mammary carcinoma.
the development of a model system of spontaneous ADR resistance in a solid murine tumor, and with the elucidation of its biochemical and molecular basis.
the development of an in vivo model system for the investigation of drug resistance mechanisms in human tumors and the development of new therapeutic strategies to circumvent these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 16C tumor model does not exhibit the mdr phenotype and that the resistance mechanism in the 16C system is unrelated to P-gp expression and function, but rather appears to be related to the GSH detoxifying system.
the resistance of 16 C/ADR to ADR is not related to the overexpression of the 170 P-gp, but is related to an increase in GSH detoxifying enzymes, which are known to be inducible by ADR in vitro.
the mechanism of acquired resistance to ADR in the 16C system is not related to the mdr phenotype, but appears to be related to the increased GSH detoxification capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the 16C tumor system is an excellent model for the study of the mechanism and the clinical relevance of drug resistance in solid tumors.
the 16C model of spontaneous resistance to ADR in vivo, which is characterized by a progressive increase in resistance, does not conform to the mdr phenotype.

the 16C tumor line, selected for its sensitivity, and the resistant variant, 16C/ ADRR, obtained from the tumor explant following a course of ADR, have been characterized with regard to GSH metabolism and P-glycoproteins expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the mechanism by which a solid tumor can become resistant to a drug.
the resistance to ADR is not mediated by the 170 kDa P-glycoproteiin, but is due to the elevation of the GSH detoxication system.
the resistance of 16 C/ADRR to ADR is a result of increased GSH detoxification activity, not P-gp expression.
